findings.quote: A **bar chart** uses bar length to represent magnitude. Because length is measured from a baseline, truncating the quantitative axis can exaggerate differences; a zero baseline is normally appropriate when bar lengths encode absolute magnitudes. By contrast, a **line chart** emphasizes position and change, so its vertical axis does not necessarily need to begin at zero. The scale should match the analytical purpose and make changes interpretable without distortion.
